questions.question: Is the front brake safe to use?

options.text: No, it is less powerful than the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if used properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes when you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake, but it is safe to use if you use it properly.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change. Choose a position that gives you more space and helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT prevent a friend from driving while drunk?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Keep them busy with activities to slow their drinking while they sober up.
Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Get other friends to help stop them from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: Waiting 15 minutes does not prevent drunk driving. Good ways to help include arranging a safe ride, keeping them busy with other activities, and getting friends to help apply pressure.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It damages the engine and should not be done.
It works like using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: It works like using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle the same way brakes do. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should be avoided?

options.text: No part should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best and no position should always be avoided. Choose a position that fits the riding conditions.

questions.question: What happens to a sidecar when the motorcycle accelerates?

options.text: It feels like it is falling behind.
It feels like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is unpowered weight attached to the motorcycle. When you accelerate, it feels like the sidecar is lagging behind because of its weight.

questions.question: Where is the horn button usually located on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The horn button is on the left handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up while braking, release the front brake immediately. Then apply the brake smoothly again.

questions.question: Why should you not ride directly next to a car or truck? Which reason does NOT apply?

options.text: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
The vehicle might block your escape route.
The driver may think you are trying to race them.
The driver may not see you and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may think you are trying to race them.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in their blind spot. The driver might not see you and move into your lane. It is also dangerous because the vehicle could block your way to escape from hazards.

questions.question: Which idea should NOT be used when planning a long group ride?

options.text: Plan travel segments based on the least experienced rider.
Minimize breaks to reach the destination faster.
Place inexperienced riders behind the leaders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Minimize breaks to reach the destination faster.
questions.explanation: Plan route length based on the least experienced rider's skill level. Take regular breaks to reduce fatigue. Place inexperienced riders behind experienced ones so they can be watched. Ride in a staggered formation.

questions.question: You may not need extra space between you and the car ahead if:

options.text: You cannot see past the vehicle ahead.
The weather is good and traffic is light.

questions.correctAnswerText: The weather is good and traffic is light.
questions.explanation: You need more space between you and the car ahead in bad conditions. Increase your space if the road is slippery, you cannot see past the car ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What happens if a rider refuses to take a breath test when an officer asks?

options.text: The officer must let them go.
The officer cannot use their notes in court.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their license will be suspended.
questions.explanation: Maine has an Implied Consent Law. By driving on state roads, you agree to take a breath test if asked by an officer. If you refuse, your license will be suspended for up to six years.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other rule signs are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. Riders must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, all of the following matter except:
questions.correctAnswerText: It looks nice.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT safety standards. It should fit snugly all around with no visible damage like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best formation?
questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Switch to a single-file line when turning, on curves, or entering and exiting highways.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should new riders position themselves?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: New riders should ride right behind the leader. This keeps them from falling behind, and it lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you move?
questions.correctAnswerText: Just your head.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop?

options.text: Keep your knees against the tank and look ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the tank and look ahead.
questions.explanation: For the best straight-line stop, apply the brakes smoothly and firmly. As weight moves forward, the front tire has more grip. Increase front brake pressure while decreasing rear brake pressure. Keep your knees against the tank and look ahead to stay straight.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have curved mirrors. What do these mirrors do?

options.text: They are easy to use right away.
They make cars look closer than they are.
They show a narrow view of the road.
They make cars look farther away than they are.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make cars look farther away than they are.
questions.explanation: Curved mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. But they make objects look farther away than they really are. Practice judging distances with curved mirrors if you are not used to them.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve:

options.text: Riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders who have had less than six months of experience on the motorcycle they were riding.

questions.question: When you stop, what gear should you be in?
questions.correctAnswerText: First gear
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow down or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies some rear braking when you use the front brake
Applies some front braking when you use the rear brake
Applies equal braking to both front and rear brakes when you use either one
Records how hard you brake and remembers your pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies some front braking when you use the rear brake
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system is a type of linked braking system. When you use the rear brake, it also applies some braking to the front. Check your motorcycle's owner's manual for details about your specific braking system.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when another vehicle is passing you?

options.text: In the center of the lane
On the left side of the lane
On the right side of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center of the lane
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. This discourages the other driver from returning to your lane too soon.

questions.question: How do you swerve on a motorcycle?

options.text: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn
Press the handgrip away from the direction you want to turn

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn
questions.explanation: To swerve, gently press the handgrip on the side where you want to go. To swerve left, press the left handgrip, then press the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: What is the safest way to cross angled railroad tracks?

options.text: Go straight ahead in your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Go straight ahead in your lane
questions.explanation: The safest way is to go straight in your lane. Turning to cross at a right angle can be dangerous because it might send you into another lane.

questions.question: What road sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about conditions ahead on the road.

questions.question: What should you do if road conditions require a longer stopping distance?

options.text: Have someone else ride your motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance
questions.explanation: You need more following distance if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. This is especially true on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead, or in heavy traffic. Use at least a three-second following distance.

questions.question: When the road is wet, what part of the lane should you avoid?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: Oil from cars drips onto the center of the lane. This oily strip is okay for motorcycles on dry roads, but not on wet roads. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride to the side and still stay in the center part of your lane.

questions.question: What helps drivers see you at an intersection?

options.text: Making eye contact with other drivers
Weaving back and forth in your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding with your headlight on
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at intersections. Ride in a lane position that makes it easy for oncoming traffic to see you. Keep a space cushion so you can escape if needed. Never assume another driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: What should you do if rain starts while you are riding?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars
questions.explanation: The center of the lane has oil buildup, which is slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars for better grip. Slow down on wet roads.
